resale_co.name: Certificate of Continuing Occupancy on sale or transfer (sewer / sump pump inspection, for homes on Township sewer); the Township's closing list also sends sellers to the Fire Department for the residential Certificate of Occupancy, which is the smoke and CO certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Medford Township (sewer inspection scheduled through Utility Billing / Sewer and Water); smoke and CO part by Medford Township Fire & EMS Department
resale_co.valid_for: Sump pump Certificate of Continuing Occupancy: 180 days from issue (Township Code 71-10E(1))
requirements: Homes on public sewer: inspection before closing; no sump pumps, roof drains or other drainage devices may be connected directly or indirectly to the Township sanitary sewer (Township Code 121-8)
If a bad connection cannot be removed right away, a $2,000 cash bond can be posted so the certificate can issue; it is released after the work passes inspection
Homes on public water: final water meter reading before closing
Smoke and CO certificate from the Fire Department (see fire_cert)
Homes on wells and septic systems: handled by the Burlington County Health Department, not the Township

fees.label: Certificate of continuing occupancy for sump pumps (sewer inspection on sale)
fees.quote: Certificate of continuing occupancy for sump pumps: $50. (Valid for 180 days from date of issuance.)

resale_co.how_to_apply: For homes on public water and/or sewer, call Utility Billing at (609) 654-2608 ext 303 to schedule the final water reading and the sewer inspection for settlement. For the smoke and CO certificate (the 'Certificate of Occupancy' on the Township's closing list), apply online with the Fire Department's Smoke Detector Inspection Application (see fire_cert).
resale_co.contact_title: Utility Billing (final water reading and sewer inspection)

evidence.quote: To obtain a Certificate of Occupancy please contact the Fire Department . For those units with public water and/or sewer, please contact the Utility Billing office for final meter readings and sewer inspections.
A residential smoke detector, CO Detector, and inspection is performed by the Fire Department.
For questions regarding your water & sewer bill, to schedule a final water reading or a sewer inspection for settlement or address change, please call Billing at (609) 654-2608 ext 303.

The Township of Medford shall require a certificate of continuing occupancy in accordance with the applicable Uniform Construction Code regulations on any sale or transfer of property to ensure that extraneous flow is not entering Medford's sanitary sewer system.
evidence.doc_date: Chapter 121 as amended through Ord. No. 2024-8

evidence.quote: An inspection of said properties will be conducted by the Township before a certificate of continuing occupancy is issued. It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to schedule an inspection with the Department of Neighborhood Services.
If conditions preclude the immediate disconnection of the disallowed flow, a cash bond in the amount of $2,000 shall be posted with the Township to guarantee the completion of said work.

The Township Council adopted Ordinance 2018-24 establishing an annual inspection program for 1- and 2-family residential rental buildings and premises; or at the time of change of use, ownership, or tenancy. Said inspections will be conducted by the Construction Code Office. The fee for said inspection is $200.

resale_co.notes: Changed from the last check: the Township code (ecode360 ME0295, read in full through its print view) adds a sale-tied Certificate of Continuing Occupancy for sewer connections. Section 121-8 requires it 'on any sale or transfer of property' to keep sump pumps and roof drains out of the sanitary sewer, and Section 71-10E(1) sets the fee at $50, valid 180 days (Chapter 71 adopted by Ord. No. 2023-16, amended by Ord. No. 2025-4). The code says to schedule with the 'Department of Neighborhood Services'; the Township's current Utilities page says to call Billing at (609) 654-2608 ext 303 to schedule a sewer inspection for settlement. This applies only to homes on Township sewer. There is no general Construction Office housing inspection for owner-occupied sales; Section 71-5 lists an optional '$150' certificate of continued occupancy 'at the request of the owner for change of ownership/tenant', which is a fee only, not a requirement. Rental properties are different: Ordinance 2018-24 Construction Office rental inspections ($200), a landlord registration fee ($25 in Code 71-17C; the Construction page still says $20), a Lead Safe Certificate for pre-1978 rentals, and a well water test every 5 years where applicable. Construction Office: 49 Union Street, (609) 654-2608. Water and sewer questions: (609) 654-6791 x 325.

requirements: Smoke alarm on each level including basements (not attic or crawl space), and smoke and CO alarms outside each sleeping area within 10 feet of bedrooms
Homes built before 1977: 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms; later homes: AC hard-wired alarms by year built, interconnected where required, kept in working order
Interconnected systems cannot be replaced with stand-alone battery detectors
Homes with a monitored NFPA 72 system instead of AC alarms need a certificate of compliance from a certified alarm contractor or electrician
CO alarm in the common hall outside of, and within 10 feet of, the bedroom doors; battery or plug-in is acceptable
House number visible from the public road, contrasting and bright or reflective (Township Code 51-3)
Leave alarm instruction manuals for the next owner
The online form does not list a fire extinguisher (the code article title still mentions one)

authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days before the change of occupant for the lowest fee.

fees.label: Second re-inspection or later, each (first re-inspection is free)
fees.quote: A fee of $35 shall be assessed for the second required reinspection or greater. There shall be no additional fee charged for the first reinspection.

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online Smoke Detector Inspection Application linked from medfordfire.org (property address, settlement date, time until settlement, owner, phone to set up the inspection, email for the certificate) and check each compliance box; all boxes must be checked before an inspection is scheduled. When paying by credit card, the fee amount is entered on the MuniPay form. The certificate is emailed. Inspection line (609) 953-3291.

fire_cert.notes: Medford is a municipal fire code enforcing agency (code M in the July 2026 DCA registry). The fees on the online form match Township Code Section 71-18A, read from ecode360. Note the small wording gaps: the form's choices read '10 or more', '5 to 9' and '4 or less' business days, the form fee text says 'more than 10' for the $50 tier, and the code says 'less than four' for the $161 tier, so the exact boundary days are unclear. The Township page shows the Fire Marshal's email as a protected link; bwidmann@medfordfire.org is from the state directory. Fire inspectors listed on the Township page: Nathan Brown, Nicholas Pica, John Horn, Eddie Keebler and Matt Plowman. Medford Lakes Borough is a separate town.

other_items.label: Final water meter reading and sewer inspection
other_items.detail: Homes on public water and/or sewer: call Billing at (609) 654-2608 ext 303 to schedule a final water reading or a sewer inspection for settlement.

other_items.label: Sump pump / roof drain disconnection
other_items.detail: Township Code 121-8 bars sump pumps, roof drains and other drainage from the sanitary sewer; they must be disconnected (or a $2,000 cash bond posted) before the sale certificate issues.

other_items.label: Wells and septic systems
other_items.detail: Handled by the Burlington County Health Department, 15 Pioneer Boulevard, Westampton, 609-265-5515.
